intended_object: The canonical bijection, for K algebraically closed and finitely many variables, between the zero locus V(I) ⊆ K^σ of an ideal I ⊆ K[x_σ] and the closed points (maximal ideals) of Spec(K[x_σ]/I). A point a goes to the kernel of evaluation at a; the inverse sends a closed point to its coordinates. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Vakil §3.6.9).
explanation:
The forward map sends a ∈ zeroLocus K I to the kernel of the surjective K-algebra map K[x]/I → K obtained by evaluating at a and passing to the quotient. That kernel is maximal, so it is a closed point of the prime spectrum. The inverse takes a closed point x and pulls it back to a maximal ideal of K[x]. By Mathlib's Nullstellensatz (`eq_vanishingIdeal_singleton_of_isMaximal`), this maximal ideal is the vanishing ideal of a unique point, and that point lies in V(I). Both round-trip identities are proved, so this is the standard canonical correspondence.

Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus` with k = K is exactly {x | ∀ p ∈ I, aeval x p = 0}. Closed points are characterised as maximal ideals through `PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_singleton_iff_isMaximal`.

The hypotheses `IsAlgClosed K` and `Finite σ` are really needed. Over a field that is not algebraically closed, or with infinitely many variables, some maximal ideals do not come from points of K^σ, so the map is not surjective. The restricted setting is therefore the natural one for this statement. The definition places no reducedness assumption on I, which matches the docstring.

I found no Mathlib equivalence between `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus` and `closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial σ K ⧸ I))`. A grep for equivalences involving `zeroLocus` or `closedPoints` only turned up prime-spectrum order isomorphisms, which are a different statement.
